title: Freedom before grace is bound, like sight in the dark until the object appears
source_text: IX. Ut ostendat autem quomodo homo ante gratiam arbitrium liberum habeat, etiam in spiritualibus, cum tamen ante gratiam bonum facere non possit; dicit in eo statu arbitrium hominis liberum quidem eo respectu esse: sed tamen ejus libertatem esse quasi ligatam atque impeditam: solvi autem & expediri, quum potentia proxima ad operandum per Dei gratiam praevenientem ei confertur. Atque ut eam rem illustret, Simile, inquit, aliquid experimur in potentia videndi: nam absente specie sensibili, habet homo potentiam & libertatem videndi: non enim ea species causa est libertatis, aut potentiae videndi; sed tamen potentia remota est, & libertas ligata, donec accepta specie potentia perficiatur, & in actum prodire possit.
pass_a_gloss: IX. But that he may show how man before grace has free choice, even in spiritual things, while yet before grace he cannot do good; he says that in that state the choice of man is indeed free in that respect: but yet its freedom is as it were bound and hindered: and is loosed and set free, when the proximate power for working is conferred on it through the prevenient grace of God. And that he may illustrate that matter, We experience, he says, something similar in the power of seeing: for when the sensible species is absent, man has the power and freedom of seeing: for that species is not the cause of the freedom, or of the power of seeing; but yet the power is remote, and the freedom bound, until, the species being received, the power is perfected, and can go forth into act.
pass_b_english: To show how man before grace has free choice even in spiritual things, though before grace he cannot do good, he says that in that state man's choice is indeed free in that respect, but its freedom is, as it were, bound and hindered. It is untied and released when the proximate power to act is given to it by God's prevenient grace.

He illustrates this: 'We find something like it in the power of sight. When the sensible image is absent, a man has the power and freedom to see, for that image is not the cause of the freedom or of the power of seeing. Yet the power is remote and the freedom bound until the image is received, the power is completed, and it can go out into act.'
